az_lower_wall_2.blurb: Lower Wall is a short quartzite face in the Spring Creek canyon east of Payson, at roughly 5,300 feet in the Christopher Creek Gorge area. It holds 19 routes, mostly bolted sport lines with a handful of trad climbs, in the 75 to 85 foot range. Grades are moderate: a few easy leads in the 5.7 to 5.9 range, then a thick cluster of 5.10s and a single 5.11. The wall looks northwest, which keeps it comfortable on shoulder-season mornings and early afternoons. Routes here are recent, so expect clean rock, uncrowded climbing and a good fit for climbers stepping up to the low double-digit grades.

az_sven_tower_3.blurb: Sven Tower 3 is the largest of the three Sven Towers on the east side of the McDowell Mountains, near Scottsdale and Phoenix. Nearly all of its 19 routes are trad, with one sport line, and several run to multiple pitches on a granite tower that looks out toward Fountain Hills. Difficulty starts at an easy 5.5 and climbs to a single 5.11, with the bulk of routes between 5.7 and 5.10. The east exposure means morning sun and afternoon shade, handy when the desert warms up. It suits climbers who want longer moderate adventure routes close to the city.
az_sven_tower_3.approach: From the Tom's Thumb trailhead, take the main trail a short way, then branch onto the Feldspar Trail and follow the signs toward the towers. Continue up the drainage to the saddle; Tower 3 sits below and to the right of the Apron, and a trail drops to its base.

az_whole_world_area_the.blurb: The Whole World Area is a small bouldering zone in the Groom Creek hills south of Prescott, directly across Senator Highway from The Island. It holds 19 problems clustered on a couple of boulder piles, many visible from the road, including a large slab pocked with a hueco that gives the area its name. Most lines are easy to moderate, from the lowest grades up to about V4, and the landings are generally friendly. Parking is shared with neighbouring boulders, and the pine-shaded hillside makes it a relaxed place for a short session or a warm-up before the larger boulderfields nearby.

az_west_elden_2.blurb: West Elden Bouldering lies on the west flank of Mount Elden just north of Flagstaff, where large dacite blocks are strewn below an old trad cliff. The 19 problems here span the full range, from a few easy lines up through the mid grades to a group of V8 to V10 testpieces. The stone is crimpy and rough on skin, so bring tape. Locals divide the zone into an Uptown half and a Downtown half, and many older problems are unmarked, so plan on wandering to find them. Cool summer temperatures make it a popular escape when lower crags overheat.

az_amphitheatre_the.blurb: The Amphitheatre is a bouldering pocket up Pima Canyon in South Mountain Park, on the south side of Phoenix. Its 19 problems circle a flat, enclosed bowl of granite, a few minutes beyond the warm-up wall. The spread is wide: a handful of very easy lines, a solid middle of V3 to V5, and a few harder problems reaching V8. The enclosed setting gives a sheltered, contained feel, and a visible trail leads in from the wash. It is a good stop for a mixed group with different ability levels once you have covered the entrance boulders.

az_turret_rock_and_environs.blurb: Turret Rock and Environs is a cluster of granite towers just below the Windy Point overlook on the Catalina Highway, high on Mount Lemmon above Tucson. It offers 19 routes, mostly trad with a few sport lines, ranging from beginner-friendly 5.6 leads through plenty of 5.8 to 5.10 climbing to one 5.12 pitch. Because the towers have faces pointing every direction, you can usually move around to find shade. The short walk down from the parking lot, with a little scrambling, keeps the day easy, and this is one of the more approachable crags on the mountain.
